content.value_statement: Multi-objective problems require trade-offs when objectives conflict. This skill guides pymoo setup, algorithms, constraints, visualization, and decision selection.
actual_capabilities: Select pymoo algorithms for single, multi-objective, and many-objective optimization.
Build custom ElementwiseProblem definitions with bounds, objectives, and constraints.
Use benchmark problems such as ZDT, DTLZ, WFG, Sphere, and Rastrigin.
Configure genetic operators, termination criteria, seeds, and population settings.
Visualize Pareto fronts with scatter plots, parallel coordinates, heatmaps, and petal diagrams.
Apply decision methods such as pseudo-weights and compromise programming.
limitations: The user environment must have pymoo and scientific Python dependencies installed.
Large populations or many generations can be computationally expensive.
Optimization quality depends on problem formulation and parameter tuning.
The examples focus on pymoo 0.6.x and may need updates for other versions.

use_cases.title: Balance competing design goals
use_cases.description: Find trade-offs between cost, weight, efficiency, safety, and performance in engineering design studies.

use_cases.title: Tune models with multiple metrics
use_cases.description: Optimize accuracy, latency, model size, and resource use without reducing the problem to one metric.

use_cases.title: Benchmark optimization algorithms
use_cases.description: Compare algorithms on standard problems and evaluate convergence, diversity, and Pareto front quality.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Benchmark Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pymoo to solve the ZDT1 benchmark with NSGA-II. Explain the Pareto front and key settings.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Custom Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a custom two-objective problem with two variables and bounds from 0 to 5. Show objectives, constraints, and algorithm choice.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me solve a constrained optimization problem in pymoo. Compare feasibility-first, penalty, repair, and constraint-as-objective approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Algorithms and Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare NSGA-II, NSGA-III, and MOEA/D for my problem. Recommend settings and a decision method for choosing one solution.

output_examples.input: I need a Pareto front for cost and performance.
output: Defines population size, generation limit, and seed.
Explains how to inspect the resulting trade-off front.
Suggests a scatter plot and preference-based final selection.

output_examples.input: I have five objectives and need readable plots.
output: Explains why many-objective problems need diversity guidance.
Suggests parallel coordinates and normalized objective ranges.

output_examples.input: My constraints produce few feasible designs.
output: Checks whether constraints use the expected pymoo formulation.
Suggests feasibility-first handling before penalty methods.
Recommends repair operators or specialized constrained algorithms when needed.

best_practices: Normalize objective scales before comparing Pareto solutions.
Set a seed and record population size, generations, and termination criteria.
Visualize fronts before selecting a final design.
anti_patterns: Using NSGA-II for many-objective problems without considering NSGA-III.
Treating one Pareto point as best without stated preferences.
Ignoring constraint formulation and feasibility checks.

faq.question: What is pymoo best for?
faq.answer: It is best for evolutionary optimization, especially problems with multiple conflicting objectives and Pareto trade-offs.

faq.question: When should I use NSGA-II?
faq.answer: Use NSGA-II for two or three objectives when you need a diverse Pareto front.

faq.question: When should I use NSGA-III?
faq.answer: Use NSGA-III for four or more objectives, where reference directions help maintain diversity.

faq.question: Can this skill handle constraints?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers feasibility-first handling, penalties, repair operators, and constraint-as-objective methods.

faq.question: Does it choose the final solution automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide decision methods, but final selection depends on user preferences.

faq.question: Does it install pymoo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation commands, but users should approve package installation in their environment.
